title: Onramp Wizard Pathway — quick integration sketch
content:
Problem statement:
- New developer sign-ups are high but first-call-to-success (sending a real inference request and receiving a valid response) has a big drop-off. We need a lightweight, opinionated guided flow that gets a user from signup -> API key -> working request in <10 minutes, with measurable telemetry hooks.

Hypothesis:
- If we provide a focused 'Onramp Wizard' that detects user intent (embeddings, chat, simple generation) and scaffolds the exact minimal resources (sample prompt, SDK snippet, model choice, payload templates), then more devs will reach a working integration and conversion to paid.

Target user personas:
- Indie devs / hobbyists: want copy/paste SDK examples and minimal config.
- Product engineers (PLG): want reproducible examples and quick ability to test with sample data.
- Platform integrators: want templates for server-side, security hints (KMS, env variables).

Goals / success metrics (MVP):
- Increase 'first successful API call' rate within 24h of signup from 28% -> 50% (6 weeks baseline).
- Time to first token returned median < 8 minutes from signup completion.
- Track conversion lift: trial->paid conversion +5% for cohorts that used wizard.
- Qualitative: NPS / feedback prompt shows 70% find the flow helpful.

User flow (MVP):
1) Entry points: onboarding email CTA, Console landing, Quickstart button in docs.
2) Small modal asks: "What are you trying to build?" (three options: Chat assistant, Simple text generation, Embeddings/search).
3) Based on choice, wizard scaffolds:
   - Model suggestion (one recommended model + cheaper fallback)
   - Minimal SDK snippet (JavaScript + Python) with placeholders filled (apiKey from console)
   - A runnable 'Try it' runner in-browser (sandbox) that executes one call and shows structured response + cost estimation.
4) If user opts, wizard pushes a short 'integration checklist' to console: create env var, add rate-limits, see token usage dashboard.
5) End screen: shareable snippet & 'save as template' for project.

Core components needed:
- Frontend: modal/wizard UI in Console, templating engine for code snippets, in-browser sandbox runner (secure iframe + ephemeral key).
- Backend: ephemeral key generation (scoped, short-lived), usage telemetry endpoints for funnel tracking, small service to render sample payloads and run dry-run executions against dedicated lightweight sandbox account.
- SDK: tiny helper to swap in ephemeral key and handle CORS for in-browser runner (or use server proxy).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Walkthrough for three intents with working JS and Python snippets that return a 200 with expected response structure.
- Telemetry emits events: wizard_started, intent_chosen, snippet_copied, sandbox_run_success, saved_template.
- Security: ephemeral keys expire <15 minutes; sandbox requests cannot access customer data or billing.
- UX: flow completeable without reading docs, single modal with <4 screens.

Open questions / implementation tradeoffs:
- Sandbox architecture: run requests against hosted API using a single shared sandbox project (easier) vs spinning ephemeral accounts per user (more isolation but heavier ops).
- Cost exposure: show estimated token cost before run — need to compute quickly from model profiling. Potential mismatch = confusion.
- Which models to recommend? Default to a mid-cost, high-stability model; add a "cheaper" checkbox that swaps to quantized variant.
- Should the wizard write a commit-ready config (Dockerfile/env) or just snippets? MVP: snippets only.

Edge cases / risks:
- Abuse of ephemeral sandbox for spamming prompts -> rate-limit, captcha gating.
- Users who need enterprise features (VPC, private key rotation) will be frustrated — provide clear path to Dedicated/Private onboarding.
- Analytics bias: users who are already more likely to convert might choose wizard; need A/B randomization.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (week 0–2): prototype modal + static snippets, manual tracked experiments with 50 internal testers.
- Phase 1 (week 3–6): enable sandbox runner + telemetry; soft launch to 10% of new signups.
- Phase 2 (week 7–10): full rollout + front-page console banner; instrumented A/B experiment for conversion.

Experiment ideas / measurements:
- A/B: show wizard vs docs quickstart vs no prompt. Measure time-to-first-success and trial conversion.
- Funnel retention: where do users drop out — code copy, key creation, sandbox-run fail? Use event breakdown.
- Variant: "template for SaaS chat" vs "blank slate" — which has higher conversion?

Developer notes / TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Spike: ephemeral key service design (SRE + security) — owner: Noah (JIRA DX-408).
- [ ] UX mockups for three-intent modal — owner: Tess.
- [ ] Sandbox runner POC using public-safe model + rate-limit — owner: me.
- [ ] Telemetry schema: define event payloads and destinations (Amplitude / Snowflake) — owner: Priya.

Notes to self / rough prioritization:
- Keep path friction minimal: centralize key copy button, auto-inject sample input, pre-fill with short example content.
- Avoid large surface area (no server templates for MVP).
- Decide model recommendations from applied-ml team: ask Sanjay for profiling numbers.

Mock UX copy snippets (for modal):
- Title: "Get a working request in <10 minutes"
- Step label: "Choose your starter"
- Buttons: "Try in browser", "Copy JS", "Copy Python", "Save template"
- Try screen note: "This runs on a restricted sandbox account and will not access private data."

Metrics / dashboard needs:
- New funnel dashboard: funnel events + conversion per cohort, sandbox-run success rate, median time to first token.
- Heatmap: which snippet copied most (JS vs Python).

References / related docs:
- Quickstart prototype slides: GH:github.com/redwood-inference/design/quickstart-wizard-slides
- Prior research: Customer interview notes (contrib: research/2025-onboarding-interviews.md)

Final thoughts:
- If this works, it's a strong lever for PLG velocity — reduces friction and gives clear instrumentation to optimize developer conversions.
- Keep scope tight and instrument early.

Unresolved questions to bring to weekly product sync:
- Budget for sandbox runs (who absorbs cost for free trial sandbox?).
- Legal / security sign-off for ephemeral key model.

Version history:

- 2026-03-10: updated rollout timeline and open questions
